h1: Can a brewing course help you get a job?
title: Can a brewing course help you get a job? | Craft Beer School
desc: What a brewing course can and cannot do for your job search, with no promises: knowledge, practice, vocabulary and guidance on where to look next.
teaser: A course can prepare you for the conversation. It cannot hand you the job. Here is what it really does.
standfirst: Many people ask whether a brewing course leads to a job. The honest answer is that a course helps you prepare. The job still depends on you, the brewery and the market. Here is where a course helps and where it does not.
sections: What we can say and what we cannot

We will be direct. No brewing course, ours included, guarantees a job or an internship. Breweries hire for their own reasons, at their own time. A certificate does not change that. What we can do is teach you properly, give guidance and recommend opportunities where possible.

So the better question is this: what does a course change about you as a candidate? There are four real answers.
You learn the language of the brewhouse

In an interview or a trial day, the people around you use words like OG, FG, IBU, mash pH and CIP without thinking. If you have not met these terms, you spend the day catching up. A course gives you the vocabulary and the numbers behind it. For example, a mash held at 62 to 65 °C gives a drier beer and 68 to 70 °C gives more body. Mash pH sits in a 5.2 to 5.6 window. Knowing that is the difference between nodding and following.
You find out if you like the work

This is the most useful thing a course can do and the least advertised. Brewing is heavy, wet and repetitive. Cleaning is most of the day. Some people discover they love it and some discover they love drinking beer far more than making it. Better to learn that in a week than after you have left a job.

The 1-Day Super Intensive Craft Beer Course (₹25,000, in person, in Pune, Delhi, Gurugram or Bengaluru) is built for exactly this test. You see and do a full brew day in a working microbrewery.
You get practice you can talk about

Employers want evidence you can do the basics. Brewing Fundamentals (4 weeks, ₹5,999) has you build a 20 L recipe with target OG, IBU and colour. You also calculate ABV from your own gravity readings. You also learn to clean and sanitise like a professional brewery. You can describe that work in an interview, which is stronger than saying you are interested.

The 1-Month Intensive Brewing Excellence Course goes further. It runs 48 contact hours in a partner microbrewery with QC lab access. It ends with a complete brew of your own. It also includes internship recommendations and career guidance. Those are recommendations and guidance, not placements, so please read them that way.
You see the roles that exist

Many beginners think the only job is head brewer. A brewery also needs people for the cellar, packaging, quality, taproom and sales. When you look at openings, read what each one actually asks for. A cellar role may want comfort with heavy lifting, cold rooms and early starts. A packaging role may want care with hygiene and counting. A quality role may want someone happy with a pH meter and a notebook. A course cannot decide which suits you, but it lets you ask better questions when you speak to a brewery. Ask what a normal day looks like and who you would learn from. Ask what the brewery would want you to be able to do in your first month. Those answers tell you more than any title.

Our guides on jobs in a brewery, brewery internships in India and the assistant brewer job describe them without hype.

• Hospitality or sales, wanting to talk about beer with confidence: Brewing Fundamentals.
  • Weighing up a brewing career: the 1-Day Super Intensive course first.
  • Already working in a brewery and wanting to move up: Advanced Brewing Science (6 weeks, online, ₹12,999).
  • Ready to commit to the full route: the 1-Month Intensive.

If you are comparing a degree against a short course, read brewing degree vs short course.
What a course does not do

A course will not replace time in a brewery. It will not decide how many vacancies there are in your city. It will not make a brewery hire you. Treat it as preparation that gets you into a better conversation. Many brewers still start by volunteering or working a taproom shift, then learn on the job. A course sits alongside that route and can shorten the learning, nothing more.

Before you pay for anything, find two or three breweries near you and ask what they look for in a new hire. Then tell us your background and the roles you are aiming at. We will suggest a course only if one fits. We will say so if it does not.
faqs: Will a brewing course guarantee me a job?
No. No course can promise a job or an internship. A course builds knowledge and practice. We offer guidance and recommend opportunities where possible.
Do employers ask for a brewing certificate?
Requirements differ from one brewery to another, so ask the employer. A certificate shows you have completed structured learning, but it is one part of a conversation.
Does the 1-Month Intensive include an internship?
It includes internship recommendations and career guidance. It does not guarantee an internship or a placement.
Can I start with a cheaper option?
Yes. Beer for Starters is a one-hour online course for ₹199. Safety in Brewing is a free one-week online course.
